subject: A question about parameter estimation and coverage in a Bayesian inference framework

messages.author: 92467f99580efdc0
messages.subject: A question about parameter estimation and coverage in a Bayesian inference framework
parts: I've recently finished a simulation where I generated many data sets with known, constant parameter values. I analyzed the simulated data with a method that estimates the data-generating parameters in JAGS. In addition to looking at things like bias, I recorded the proportion of BCIs that contained the true values.  Is this anything like coverage in classical inference?  Can a Bayesian use a frequentist view of probability in this way? BTW, in many simulations, nominal levels were not attained.  I attribute this result to non-asymptotic properties of the small data sets I analyzed, perhaps the use of poor (non-proper) priors, and the most obvious effect of parameter bias.  Any thoughts on this matter would be greatly appreciated.

messages.author: c3165650d54dd207
messages.subject: Re: A question about parameter estimation and coverage in a Bayesian inference framework
parts:
Hi Brian,
There is no particular consensus on whether applying frequentist ideas to Bayesian model evaluation is "best practice" but a lot of people do it and I think it is useful for assessing whether a model is going to be useful in practice.  It can also be useful for rooting out pernicious bugs in your code...  But you're right, use of different priors (especially informative ones) make such assessments difficult to interpret at times.  

 If you're interested in getting opinions of statisticians much better than myself, perhaps do a google search for 'calibrated Bayes.'    

Cheers, Paul
